title: Understanding the Bias-Variance Tradeoff
text: The bias-variance tradeoff is a fundamental concept in machine learning that helps us understand the sources of error in our models. It involves decomposing the expected squared error into three components: variance, bias squared, and irreducible error.

title: Sources of Randomness
text: When considering the bias-variance tradeoff, we account for different sources of randomness. These include the randomness in the data, the randomness in the model selection, and the randomness in the feature selection.

title: Feature Engineering and Randomness
text: Consider whether the arbitrary choice of features during feature engineering contributes to the randomness we account for in the bias-variance tradeoff.
